reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the Invoice resource context, the full local StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate, selected R4/R6 Invoice StructureDefinition elements and terminology artifacts, and the listed shared behavior context. Direct behavior findings were absent. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings were treated as context only because the assigned resource is `Invoice`, not `Resource` or `DomainResource`.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 Invoice is trial-use at FMM 0, so the compatibility burden is weaker than for mature or normative content. That softens the standards-stability objection, but it does not make financial, audit, billing, or generated-model breaks irrelevant when a low-cost compatible design appears available.

overall.oneLineConclusion: Invoice keeps its resource identity, but R6 introduces a targeted migration program around posting-date naming, price-component modeling, and price-component terminology.

reasoning.thesisMd: `Invoice` is not removed or replaced, and most of the resource shape survives. However, serious implementations cannot treat R6 as a mostly drop-in validation update: `date` is renamed to `creation`, required price-component terminology no longer accepts R4 `deduction`, and Invoice-local price components are normalized to `MonetaryComponent`. That is enough for a targeted migration program, but not enough to say compatibility no longer matters.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a moderate targeted remodel rather than a major model redesign. The central migration work is concentrated in invoice timing and monetary components: rename/map posting date, review deduction-versus-discount semantics, regenerate models and profiles for `MonetaryComponent`, and write down-conversion rules for R6-only billing/service period fields and widened references. The resource identity, line item backbone, required `chargeItem[x]`, issuer cardinality, and many common child elements remain recognizable.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a migration program is already needed, some local chores are unavoidable once the R6 model is accepted. Still, compatibility leverage remains meaningful. Keeping the old posting-date wire name, retaining `deduction` as a deprecated required-bound code, or restoring explicit `ChargeItem` target computability are low- or moderate-cost preservation choices compared with asking all implementers to add transforms and business review.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest avoidable breaks are not the additive R6 fields. `Invoice.date` and `Invoice.creation` have the same type, cardinality, and posting-date definition, so retaining `date` or providing a transition alias would preserve old instances with little semantic cost. The `deduction` removal is more domain-sensitive because R4 had both `deduction` and `discount`; preserving `deduction` as deprecated would allow gradual convergence while avoiding forced financial classification decisions at validation time. For `chargeItem[x]`, retaining `Reference(ChargeItem)` or listing explicit additional targets would preserve computable validation clarity unless R6 intentionally wanted arbitrary references.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding was assigned to `Invoice`. The shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings remain relevant to generic FHIR server migration planning, but they are not Invoice-specific evidence and were not used to raise the Invoice resource-level conclusion.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate's `Partial` major migration judgment, `moderate-targeted-remodel` shape, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration` posture are directionally right. My independent review reaches the same overall result, but the reason is not the count alone: the material point is that the hard breaks cluster around central billing/date and monetary semantics while several other findings are additive or reverse-conversion chores.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural deltas because they are visible in the primary R4/R6 StructureDefinitions and CodeSystems. Confidence is lower for design intent and prevalence because no official rendered diff, ballot rationale, or production Invoice corpus was supplied; the `chargeItem[x]` target-profile removal is especially intent-sensitive because the narrative still names ChargeItem.

findingConsiderations.title: Invoice.date was renamed to Invoice.creation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the clearest avoidable R4-to-R6 instance break. The R4 and R6 elements describe the same posting-date concept with the same `dateTime` shape, but the wire name changes. For billing, audit, and generated FHIRPath/profile paths, a rename transform is required unless the base design preserves `date`.

findingConsiderations.title: Price component code `deduction` was removed from the required type binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: A required-bound R4 `deduction` value becomes invalid in R6. Because R4 had both `deduction` and `discount`, migration may require financial policy judgment rather than a purely mechanical replacement. Retaining `deduction` as deprecated would be a plausible low-cost compatibility measure.

findingConsiderations.title: Invoice price components now use the shared MonetaryComponent datatype
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This drives the targeted migration program because generated classes, profile paths, and any R4 `modifierExtension` on the Invoice-local backbone need review. The shared datatype goal is coherent, so this is mostly a local migration chore once the redesign is accepted, but it is still part of why migration is not optional.

findingConsiderations.title: Invoice.lineItem.chargeItemReference no longer has a computable ChargeItem-only target profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This does not invalidate R4 ChargeItem references, so it does not make R4-to-R6 migration unavoidable. It still matters for standards review because it weakens computable validation of a required billing line-item reference while the narrative continues to describe ChargeItem.

findingConsiderations.title: Invoice.issuer can now reference Practitioner and PractitionerRole as well as Organization
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a forward-compatible target widening for R4 Organization issuers. It creates R6-to-R4 export and consumer-assumption work, but it is not an R4-to-R6 instance break and should not drive the resource-level migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Invoice.period[x] for the billing date or period
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional addition is useful R6 expressiveness and does not break R4 instances moving forward. It only requires local down-conversion policy or an extension strategy when exporting richer R6 content back to R4.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds Invoice.lineItem.serviced[x] for line-item service date or period
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is another optional R6 addition. R4 line items remain valid in R6, and the compatibility concern is reverse-conversion loss rather than a base R4-to-R6 break.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This representative shared Resource behavior finding may affect generic servers handling Invoice resources, but it is not assigned directly to `Invoice`. It was kept as migration context and not used to score the Invoice StructureDefinition-level conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit whether `Invoice.date` should be retained as the base posting-date wire name, or at least supported as a deprecated transition element, because `creation` appears to be a same-semantics rename.

Review the financial semantics of removing required-bound `deduction`; if `discount` is intended as the replacement, consider retaining `deduction` as deprecated and publishing an explicit ConceptMap/migration note.

Confirm the intent of the unconstrained R6 `Invoice.lineItem.chargeItem[x]` Reference. If arbitrary references are not intended, restore `Reference(ChargeItem)` or list the intended additional target profiles.

Publish explicit R4/R6 mapping guidance for `MonetaryComponent`, `period[x]`, `lineItem.serviced[x]`, and widened `issuer` targets so implementers can separate unavoidable model migration from avoidable compatibility loss.

caveats: No official rendered diff, ballot rationale, or issue history was available, so standards intent is inferred from computable artifacts.

No production Invoice corpus or common profile inventory was supplied, so prevalence of `date`, `deduction`, price-component modifier extensions, and non-Organization issuer requirements is estimated.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were reviewed as context only and not counted as direct Invoice behavior breaks.
